formal_condition: Identifiability requires that there exist input histories H_attack and H_benign such that B0(H_attack) == B0(H_benign) within numerical epsilon, but Q(H_attack) != Q(H_benign).

test_setup.H_attack_description: 1 attack pulse at A=0.4100 followed by 38 rest steps at A=0.1656

Family_A_Count_Based.notes: Q_attack=1, Q_benign=0. Successfully separates aliased states.

Family_B_Exponential_Decay.notes: Q_attack=1.633263, Q_benign=1.628803. Delta=0.00445981. Note: with linear f, Q decays at rate 0.90^38 ~ 0.016, rendering residual separation weak unless rho is high.

Family_C_Threshold_Offset.notes: Q_attack=0.010388, Q_benign=0.000000. Because benign traffic produces f(0.1656)=0, Q_benign is strictly 0.0, while Q_attack retains the decaying residual of the attack pulse.

Family_D_Inter_Arrival.notes: Q_attack captures the event arrival; Q_benign is 0.0.

Family_E_Rate_Based.notes: For W=20 after 38 rest steps, the attack event has already exited the sliding window, so Q_attack=0 and Q_benign=0. FAILS identifiability once rest exceeds window W!

repeated_cycle_identifiability.description: After 8 complete cycles of Cycle A (1 attack + 10 rest each = 88 steps), B0 states are identical to 88 pure rest steps at convergence.

Family_C_8cycles_rho_095.note: Under rho=0.95, each cycle adds f(0.41) = 0.5693 and decays by 0.95^11 = 0.5688 per cycle. Steady periodic peak Q reaches f / (1 - 0.5688) = 1.320, while benign rest Q remains strictly 0.0.
